items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: I wrote a tune and carried it down to Mayo Williams who was with Decca... I gave it to Mayo Williams. He was with Paramount Records. Mayo liked it, and he said, I'm going to give it to General Martin to record.

ctx.x: Did you do any recording? No.

I made, yes, I hate to tell about it. No, we had, during the time that we had this little string band, I wrote a tune and carried it down to Mayo Williams who was with Decca. And Mayo said, who is that, whipping that guitar? I said, that's me playing guitar. I said, but that's a tenor guitar. I said, I can't play a Spanish guitar. So he says, well, he says, you ought to get a guitar. I said, you know, make them better and bigger now. So I says, he said, but anyhow, I want you to make a record. He said, George…
I've gotten a lot of early Georgia and one of these days you'll go over them. Yeah. But this was in the mid to early 30s. Yes.
